transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood CSM), Jared Morales (Oceanic CISO), Mina Park (Cloud Sec Eng), Dylan Hughes (IT Ops), Sara Ito (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick security review focused on audit logs and admin activity: what events Redwood captures, export options (S3, syslog, SIEM), retention defaults and configurable retention for Dedicated/Private, encryption/KMS handling, immutability/tamper evidence, and integration points for Oceanic's Splunk deployment. Next steps agreed to share export examples, retention pricing, and a pilot plan.

Topics covered:
- Events captured (log inventory)
- Export and streaming options
- Retention and storage (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- Encryption and KMS/HSM integration
- RBAC and log access controls
- Compliance artifacts (SOC 2/ISO)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll give a quick run through on audit logs and admin activity, primarily what we capture, how you can export it and retention models. samir will jump into a couple of the technical bits.
[00:18] Jared: perfect thanks avery, um Oceanic is looking to understand what exactly gets logged before we start the pilot — especially admin actions around keys and model rollouts.
[00:28] Samir: sure, high-level, we capture three buckets: control plane admin events, data-plane inference events metadata, and system events. control plane includes user and service principal logins, role changes, RBAC policy updates, SSO/SCIM provisioning events, API key creates/rotations/deletes, model version deploy/undeploy, rollout actions (canary start/finish), config changes, and dedicated capacity assignments.
[00:48] Mina: when you say model deploy, does that include the model config (like quantization or instance profile) or just the event that it happened?
[00:56] Samir: good q. we log the event + the visible config snapshot — not the model weights, obviously — so things like model id, version, quantization profile name, instance type, and rollout id are included.
[01:05] Dylan: what about KV cache or prefix cache flushes? we've had incidents where stale cache impacted outputs.
[01:14] Samir: yes we log cache-related admin events — cache flush/eviction calls, manual KV deletes, and automated cache policy changes (thresholds). they show up as admin_activity.cache.flush with timestamps and actor.
[01:28] Sara: can you confirm whether these logs include any request-level content? like prompts or model outputs — we can't send PII to third parties.
[01:36] Avery: short answer: no full user prompts or model output are stored in control-plane audit logs by default. inference telemetry contains high level metrics (token counts, latency buckets, request ids) but bodies are redacted in hosted by default; for private deployments customers can opt-in to richer telemetry but we recommend redaction and legal review.
[01:56] Jared: good. what about pii that might leak in filenames or artifacts?
[02:02] Samir: we have patterns to mask file names in logs and we also support custom scrubbing pipelines before export. we'll include the scrub config examples in the playbook.
[02:14] Avery: for export options, we support push and pull models — scheduled exports to S3 (AWS), Azure Blob, GCS; streaming to syslog or a SIEM via syslog/HEC (for Splunk), and BigQuery streaming for analytics teams. we also support webhook delivery for real-time downstream systems.
[02:36] Mina: is streaming encrypted in transit?
[02:39] Samir: yep TLS 1.2/1.3 for HTTPS endpoints, syslog over TLS, and all S3 uploads use HTTPS + server-side encryption if you want it.
[02:49] Dylan: do you have a connector for Splunk specifically?
[02:52] Avery: yes we've got a certified Splunk HEC example in the docs and a community lambda for transforming to your index patterns, we'll send the exact config.
[03:03] Sara: retention — what's default for hosted? can we set longer retention for logs older than 90 days?
[03:10] Samir: hosted defaults to 90 days of audit logs in the console; exports can be set up to hold them in your S3/GCS indefinitely. for Dedicated we can configure longer on-disk retention (up to 3 years) and for Private deployments on-prem or VPC, retention is customer controlled — technically unlimited but T&Cs apply. for regulated customers we offer retention add-ons up to 7 years with WORM (write once read many) compliance in Dedicated/Private.
[03:39] Jared: WORM sounds promising — is that tamper-evident?
[03:43] Samir: WORM plus cryptographic signing for export bundles. we provide manifest files and HMAC signatures; if you need enterprise-grade immutability we can recommend stamping to S3 Object Lock + Glacier Vault Lock practices.
[03:55] Mina: curious about access controls: who in our org can view logs in the Redwood console? can you integrate with our SSO and enforce RBAC?
[04:03] Avery: yes SSO via SAML/SCIM for provisioning, and role-based access controls. by default, only users with the Audit Reader or Admin roles can access plain audit entries. we can scope policies down to routes (e.g., only view API key rotations, not content-level telemetry) and bind to groups synced from your IdP.
[04:22] Dylan: and KMS — do you manage keys or can we bring our own?
[04:26] Samir: both. hosted can use Redwood-managed keys or customer-managed keys in your cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS). for Private we support HSM integrations and enterprise KMS workflows. all audit artifacts at rest are encrypted with AES-256 and envelope encryption is used when customer-managed keys are configured.
[04:46] Sara: do you rotate keys automatically? what's the policy?
[04:50] Samir: we recommend rotation every 90 days; Redwood-managed rotate automatically per our policy and the rotation event is logged. customer-managed keys follow your KMS rotation policies — we log the KMS key id change and any failed encrypt/decrypt operations.
[04:59] Jared: how do you handle exports for cross-region compliance? Oceanic requires logs to stay in-region for certain customers.
[05:06] Avery: you can pin export destinations to specific regions, and for Private deployments we can ensure data residency by keeping control plane and exported artifacts inside your VPC region. for hosted, we offer region controls (US, EU) and can provide contractual commitments for region residency.
[05:20] Mina: are there pre-built retention policies we can apply per-project or per-tenant?
[05:25] Samir: yes — retention policies are attachable to projects/tenants — you can say project-alpha keep 180 days, project-beta keep 7 years, and we enforce via lifecycle jobs.
[05:36] Dylan: curious about volume and cost; will streaming all admin events be expensive?
[05:40] Avery: admin events are low volume compared to inference tokens — typically a few hundred MBs per month for most orgs. cost is mostly for long-term storage and SIEM ingestion; we'll share sample estimates in the follow-up.
[05:52] Jared: audit log format — is it JSON? what fields can we expect?
[05:56] Samir: JSON, newline-delimited. key fields: timestamp, event_type, actor_id (user/service), actor_ip, resource (resource_type/resource_id), action, context (snapshot of config), request_id, region, and a diff payload for changes. we'll share a sample schema.
[06:16] Mina: do you support immutable sequence numbers or append-only logs for forensics?
[06:20] Samir: each record has a monotonic sequence number and request_id; for stronger guarantees we can publish signed manifests per daily bundle.
[06:29] Sara: SOC 2 evidence — can you provide logs for auditors?
[06:33] Avery: yes we provide SOC 2 artifacts and can run ad-hoc exports for auditors. we maintain an access log of who pulled what and when. we'll include SOC 2 Type II summary in the packet.
[06:46] Jared: any caveats around redaction or PII retention in exports?
[06:50] Samir: exports are a raw dump of audit events unless you route through our scrubbing pipeline; if you're exporting to your own bucket you control lifecycle and scrubbing. we recommend a preprocessing lambda if you need to strip PII before ingest to your SIEM.
[07:03] Dylan: about real-time alerting — can audit events trigger webhooks or alerts?
[07:07] Samir: yes, you can configure rules to forward specific event types (e.g., admin role change, key rotation failure) as webhook, PagerDuty, or SIEM events.
[07:17] Mina: how long does it take to enable exports? is it a change window?
[07:21] Avery: for hosted, exports are generally set up in a few hours once credentials are provided; for Dedicated/Private there's a short ops window depending on networking and firewall rules.
[07:31] Jared: demo request — can you show an example of an audit record and an export manifest?
[07:35] Samir: yeah i'll pull a sanitized sample now — give me 10 secs.
[07:45] Speaker 1: [crosstalk, typing sounds]
[07:52] Samir: okay here's a line-delimited JSON sample i pasted in the doc: event_type: "admin_activity.role.grant", timestamp, actor_id, resource: "project/alpha/role/rdx", diff: {old: null, new: "audit-reader"}, request_id. again sanitized.
[08:10] Mina: looks good. can the diff include numeric quotas we changed? we've had trouble tracking who modified rate limits.
[08:16] Samir: yes diffs include numeric fields. we also support a change_reason field if you want to force users to provide justification on certain sensitive changes.
[08:27] Avery: one more note on retention & legal holds: we support ad-hoc holds which suspend lifecycle deletion for selected datasets — useful for investigations.
[08:39] Sara: any limits on export size or rate?
[08:42] Samir: no hard limits for exports but very large exports are chunked; for SIEM ingestion you might prefer streaming to avoid backfills.
[08:51] Dylan: is there an event for failed auth attempts or brute force?
[08:55] Samir: yes auth failures, MFA failures, and suspicious sign-in heuristics are logged; we can tag severity and pipe high-severity to your SOC.
[09:05] Jared: governance question — who on Redwood can access customer audit logs?
[09:09] Avery: access is strictly limited — only support engineers with a logged-for-access request can view customer logs and every access is logged with reason and duration. we can provide access policies for your security review.
[09:22] Mina: can we get a sample of the ACL/role definitions?
[09:25] Avery: yes we'll share an RBAC mapping doc that ties role names to permissions.
[09:30] Sara: one last question — what about chain of custody for exports? is there an attestable chain?
[09:36] Samir: we generate export manifests that include hashes and signatures and we can optionally deliver via SFTP/HTTPS with signed receipts; for Dedicated we can tape the manifests into your internal chain-of-custody tooling.
[09:47] Jared: great. recap and next steps please.
[09:50] Avery: recap — we'll send: 1) audit log schema and sample records, 2) export playbook including Splunk HEC config and syslog over TLS examples, 3) retention/pricing options for hosted/dedicated/private, 4) SOC2 artifact packet. Samir will propose pilot dates and sample config. customer to confirm SIEM destination and retention requirements.
[10:11] Mina: ok that'll work, thanks.
[10:14] Dylan: thanks all, we'll get staging creds to you by monday.
[10:18] Avery: awesome thanks everyone.

End of meeting.
